brief.text: Cluster thesis INTACT (mid), live 2026-09-15; downgraded 09-14 from strengthening because the China-controls tax on front-end tools falls unevenly. The -6% cluster day (09-14) was multiple compression from the Amodei essay and FOMC hike odds; TSMC August revenue +53.3% YoY, ASML FY26 guide EUR 43-45B and AMAT's record Q3 stand. Ladder: TSM > KLAC > TER > ASML > AMAT; leader TSM, laggard AMAT. Margin pool moving toward TSM/CoWoS and KLAC process control (a hypothesis). Falsifier: order push-outs on ASML 10-14, TSMC 10-15 or TER 10-22 calls, TSMC September revenue below +25% YoY, or ASML Q3 bookings below Q2. KEY: Intact (mid), 2026-09-15 [secondary]; Ladder TSM > KLAC > TER > ASML > AMAT; AMAT leaves laggard slot if 11-13 print narrows China hit below $600M; ASML rises to rank 2 if Q3 bookings beat with China below 20%; Bench: AMKR, LRCX (partial substitute for AMAT). OPEN: Does TSMC September revenue (~10-09) hold above +25% YoY?; Does ASML Q3 net bookings (10-14) exceed Q2?; Does KLAC disclose China above 30% on 10-29?.

live_facts: [4f65ed434ee6] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,AMD,QCOM (2026-09-21): The AI Semis/Fabs cluster mixes tool/foundry SELLERS (TSM, ASML, AMAT, KLAC, TER) with fabless silicon BUYERS (AMD, QCOM). The playbook's six differentiators are all seller-side axes, so AMD and QCOM cannot be ranked on them and must be ranked on a single applicable axis each, stated as such. Same defect class as G98 (NBIS in Compute/Hyperscaler). Until the cluster is split, its percent-of-equity figure overstates true semicap/fab exposure by roughly 4.4pp.

[1751cf07f205] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,TSM (2026-09-21): Ladder scoring datapoint: the 09-15 AI Semis/Fabs ladder (leader TSM, laggard AMAT) was WRONG in both slots over 09-15 -> 09-21 - AMAT +8.11% (+0.26pp vs SMH) beat TSM +5.93% (-1.92pp vs SMH), and the best toolmaker was TER (+11.70%, +3.85pp), which had been ranked 3 of 5. The ordering's middle beat its ends. Four sessions is not a verdict on method, but it is the second consecutive window in which the TSM leader call has not paid, so a third failure through 2026-10-15 should force the leader slot to be re-argued from the packaging axis or vacated.

[04ad6c128cea] fact AI Memory/Storage,AI Networking/Optics,AI Power/Cooling/DC Infra (2026-09-22): AI-capex chain exposure is 93.5% of invested equity as of 2026-09-22 (post STM/LLY sizing), up from prior ~89% cited in older memory notes -- the recent diversifying adds (STM, LLY) have not meaningfully changed the single-factor read; still ~19 of every 20 dollars tied to the same AI-datacenter capex cycle.

[9b3b443cf27b] fact AI Semis/Fabs,KLAC,TER (2026-09-21): KLAC/TER re-judged DISTINCT on 2026-09-21 after a second near-identical-move screen (0.3pp return gap, 1.0pp ATR gap). The decisive business argument is cycle timing, not product: front-end process control leads the tool-up, back-end test lags wafer-out, and the cluster's own read_throughs file states test lags the front end - so a synchronous 1-month move is shared-macro, not a shared bet. This is the second consecutive run the screen has flagged them and the second distinct verdict.

[fdcc57a48cdb] fact AI Semis/Fabs,QCOM (2026-09-21): QCOM's AI-datacenter story failed a filed-evidence test on 2026-09-21: a smith_edgar XBRL tag search for 'datacenter' returned zero concepts, and what exists is management forward targets ($5B FY27, $15B FY29, AI200 scaling, AI250 sampling 2027) against a ~$39.8B run-rate, with Q3 FY26 revenue $9.95B down 4% y/y. Thesis moved QCOM strengthening -> intact on this. The ladder laggard rank and the thesis downgrade were reached independently and converged - a useful check that the axis question and the thesis question are measuring the same thing when the evidence is filed rather than narrative.

[ecf55186522a] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,QCOM (2026-09-21) [secondary]: QCOM's 1-month +13.67% (rel_intra +9.26pp, second-best in cluster) has a named non-AI-capex driver: the US-China tariff/handset channel into the 09-24 summit, with CEO Amon at the White House dinner. Future runs must not read QCOM's semis-cluster outperformance as evidence of AI-capex tailwind capture; the test is whether AI200/AI250 datacenter silicon appears as a quantified revenue or backlog line, first checkable at the 10-30 FQ4 call.

[3a1fa060fd52] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,Compute/Hyperscaler (2026-09-21) [secondary]: Risk-flat rotation pairs are not dollar-for-dollar: NBIS sell $406 (12.4% stop) frees the same $50.56 risk as a $1,258 MSFT buy (4.0% stop), so the pair is a ~$851 net cash deployment and a net add to the AI-capex sleeve. While the advisory stress limit is breached (26.9% vs 20%) this is risk-flat for heat but not stress-neutral; cash-above-band and stress-limit point opposite ways and bench_diversifier produced no live row.

[14316a7d5e56] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,AMAT,ASML (2026-09-21) [secondary]: Factor threats must map to a named revenue mechanism. CXMT HBM3E was mapped onto AMAT/TER/LRCX/ASML by memory-cluster proximity with no sourced link; withdrawn 09-21 after crosscheck debate.

[c92988270737] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,AMAT,ASML (2026-09-21) [secondary]: CXMT HBM3E catalyst_threat maps by mechanism to MU/SKHY only; toolmakers (AMAT, TER, ASML) get it second-order via memory capex, which needs a within-basis ASP decline. Exposure yardsticks: AMAT China 28% of Q3 FY26 revenue (35% yr ago), DRAM +52% y/y; TER memory test $212M ~16% of Q2 2026 revenue (all secondary).

[8beb0cc1c2aa] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,AMAT (2026-09-21) [secondary]: A rank must not carry a policy leg the owning analyst has not sourced. On 2026-09-21 I promoted AMAT 5 -> 3 partly on the 09-24 Trump-Xi summit being 'positive convexity' on its largest-in-cluster China revenue at risk; catalyst then sourced the direction and found no reporting contemplating an easing of semicap-EQUIPMENT controls (the only easing on record is H200-class accelerator licensing), with the US pushing for further restrictions. AMAT went back to 4. Generalisation for future runs: a topic being ON a summit agenda is not evidence of outcome skew in either direction, and 'two-way catalyst' is a null claim unless a source establishes both legs.

[7f6d212fb1a0] lesson AI Semis/Fabs,AMAT,KLAC (2026-09-21) [secondary]: Summit 09-24 is NOT positive convexity for equipment names: SME-control skew is no-change to tighter (no public sign of easing; only H200 licensing for accelerators), tightening tail is the MATCH Act servicing ban. AMAT/KLAC strengthening rests on the Aug/Jul prints, so INTACT is the default absent new evidence by the next print; SME-control tightening on 09-24 would move AMAT to WATCH.

[4a606d66736c] fact AI Semis/Fabs (2026-09-21) [secondary]: [falsifier] TSMC guides 2027 capex flat-or-down on 2026-10-15; OR ASML Q3 net bookings print below Q2 on 2026-10-14; OR two of AMAT/KLAC/TER guide below consensus in the 2026-10-22 to 2026-11-13 window. Any one converts intact -> watch.

[8ec6d34fd5b2] fact AI Semis/Fabs (2026-09-21) [secondary]: [margin pool] moving toward Advanced packaging and test: CoWoS-class capacity (TSM), inspection/metrology steps per wafer as gate-all-around and hybrid bonding ramp (KLAC), and test seconds per die as die sizes and HBM stack counts rise (TER). The incremental AI dollar buys packaging and test capacity, not another scanner.; away from Mature-node front-end wafer tools, and lithography UNIT count. ASML's EUV ASP rises but unit growth is gated by High-NA adoption pace, so its share of each incremental AI capex dollar falls even with the monopoly fully intact. Also away from fabless silicon pricing power relative to the upstream bottleneck.

Substituting it would raise the book's exposure to the cluster's actual profit migration without adding a new geography risk the size of TSM's] Buy on evidence that packaging capacity is being added outside TSM - specifically an AMKR capacity-expansion or CoWoS-class qualification disclosure at or before its Q3 print (~2026-10-26), or TSMC's 10-15 call naming OSAT overflow. [596b43bd0a8c] fact AI Semis/Fabs,ASML,KLAC (2026-09-21) [secondary]: Margin-pool call for this cluster, stated so a future run can test it: profit is migrating TOWARD advanced packaging and test (CoWoS at TSM, inspection steps per wafer at KLAC, test seconds per die at TER) and AWAY FROM lithography UNIT count and mature-node front-end tools. [f857b529f8c5] fact AI Semis/Fabs,AMAT,TER (2026-09-21) [secondary]: Within the semicap members, China-equipment exposure is now a RANKING axis and not just a discount: catalyst states TER has no sourced China-equipment exposure and withdrew it from both the 09-24 summit and CXMT HBM3E mappings (TER's revenue is test volume tied to AI compute and SoC/wafer test, not memory ASP). With the control skew hold-or-tighter, that separates TER above AMAT on an axis that holds at any price.
